## Panama City: Miraflores Locks, IMAX and the Amador Causeway

[Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/) grew beside one of the world's most important interoceanic transport routes. On our excursion you will see the **Miraflores Locks** in operation, watch a film about the canal's construction and operation, then explore the city's historic and modern neighborhoods.

The program lasts **six hours** and is conducted with an **English-speaking guide**. Entrance tickets and excursion services are included **as specified in the selected program**. Travelers pay separately for personal expenses.

## Miraflores: how ships pass through the locks

[Miraflores Locks](/panama/place/miraflores-locks/) stand on the Pacific side of the Panama Canal. From the visitor center's observation platforms, you can watch ships passing through the lock chambers.

The operating principle is easy to observe: the water level in a chamber changes, allowing a ship to move between sections of the waterway at different elevations. The huge gates, towing mechanisms and movement of ships are impressive even for visitors with little previous interest in transport engineering.

However, **a ship passing at a particular minute is not guaranteed**. The official visitor center warns that transit schedules can change. It is therefore best to coordinate time at the observation platform with available ship-transit windows.

## IMAX: 45 minutes of Panama Canal history

The excursion includes a **3D IMAX film** about the canal's construction and operation. The confirmed runtime is **45 minutes**. The narration is provided by **Morgan Freeman**. The film is in English with Spanish subtitles.

Unlike observing the locks from the viewing platform, the film explains the canal's construction and operation in a broader historical context: the scale of excavation, engineering design and the importance of connecting the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

It is important to distinguish the **IMAX admission ticket** from additional museum visits or excursion options that may be sold separately. This program confirms the film screening and viewing of the locks as part of the agreed excursion.

## Casco Antiguo: the old town and San José Church

After the canal, the route continues through city districts, including the former American Canal Zone and **Balboa Avenue** along Panama Bay.

Next is **Casco Antiguo**, the historic quarter of squares, narrow streets and architecture from different centuries. The program includes **Plaza de Francia** and **San José Church**, famous for its golden altar.

Combining the old city center with the canal reveals how geography and commerce shaped the city. Admission to other museums and churches is not automatically included simply because they are nearby.

## Amador Causeway and the islands

The final stop is the **Amador Causeway**, connecting Panama City's waterfront with **Naos, Perico and Flamenco** islands. Rock excavated during construction of the Panama Canal was used to build the causeway.

Today, visitors can see the Pacific Ocean, ships approaching the canal and Panama City's modern skyline. The contrast is especially striking after historic Casco Antiguo: old squares give way to a broad coastal panorama.

Shopping, restaurants, independent boat rides and other Amador activities are not included among the services of the six-hour excursion.

The excursion is part of the [26-day journey through eight Central American countries](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) and suits travelers interested in history, engineering and city architecture.

## Frequently asked questions about Miraflores and Panama City

### How long is the excursion?

**Six hours**.

### Will we see ships passing through the locks?

The viewing platform overlooks the locks, but **the timing of ship passages depends on the current schedule**.

### What language is the IMAX film in?

**English with Spanish subtitles**, narrated by Morgan Freeman.

### Is Panama City's historic center included?

Yes. The itinerary visits **Casco Antiguo** and Plaza de Francia, including San José Church.

### Does the excursion stop at the Amador Causeway?

Yes. This is one of its final stops.

## Tours including “Panama City: Miraflores, IMAX and Amador”

The [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/) can be experienced in several ways: from the water, at the locks, in a museum or on a city tour. [“Panama City: Miraflores, IMAX and Amador”](/panama/panama-city/panama-city-miraflores-imax-amador/) combines observing the locks with historic neighborhoods and the waterfront. On the [26-day journey through eight Central American countries](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/), it is scheduled for the **final day of the itinerary**.

Here we have gathered {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} confirmed to use this specific six-hour excursion with IMAX and Amador. Similar names for city sightseeing do not imply identical stops: the [shorter “Miraflores, Biomuseo and Casco Viejo” excursion](/panama/panama-city/panama-miraflores-biomuseo-casco-viejo/) is a distinct product with different content.

## What the six-hour city route includes

The excursion starts at [Miraflores Locks](/panama/place/miraflores-locks/). Visitors watch ships moving through the lock chambers and learn how the canal operates. A **45-minute 3D IMAX film** is also included, in English with Spanish subtitles and narrated by Morgan Freeman. Screening times and the actual visit sequence are agreed for the date of travel.

The route then passes through the former American Canal Zone, Balboa Avenue and [Casco Viejo](/panama/place/casco-viejo/). In the old quarter, travelers explore squares and historic streets and visit San José Church with its golden altar. The journey continues to the Amador Causeway, linking Naos, Perico and [Flamenco Island](/panama/place/flamenco-island/).

| Section | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Miraflores | Locks in operation and IMAX film |
| Old town | Squares, streets and San José Church |
| Amador Causeway | Views of the bay and canal |

The standalone excursion lasts **six hours** with an English-speaking guide and admission tickets as specified in the chosen program. A separate booking is priced individually; it is not automatically an additional charge on a tour where this module is already included.

## Why it is scheduled at the end of the 26-day journey

[“Central America: 8 Countries in 26 Days”](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) starts in Mexico, passes through Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua and Costa Rica and finishes in Panama. By day 26, travelers have experienced several major historic and natural regions. The last excursion explores Panama's distinguishing features: international shipping, canal engineering and the capital's architecture.

**International flight time is the critical condition.** The excursion takes six hours and is followed by an airport transfer. An early afternoon flight may therefore be incompatible with the complete city tour. When choosing flights, coordinate not just departure time but also the end of the IMAX screening, traffic, baggage and a buffer for airport check-in.

These details matter more than trying to fit extra stops into the final day. A later flight can allow a substantial excursion; an earlier one will require agreement on the actual program. The full list of visits cannot be promised unchanged without verifying the logistics.

## How this differs from a shorter Panama trip

On the [six-day “Panama City and Gamboa” tour](/panama/tour/panama-city-gamboa-6-days/), the city is explored through another module: [“Miraflores, Biomuseo and Casco Viejo”](/panama/panama-city/panama-miraflores-biomuseo-casco-viejo/). The journey then continues to an Emberá community, [Soberanía Forest](/panama/place/soberania-national-park/) and [Monkey Island in Gatun Lake](/panama/gatun-lake/gatun-lake-monkey-island-boat/).

In the 26-day program, the main purpose of the city excursion is to **provide a meaningful conclusion to an extended multi-country journey**. The IMAX film and Amador Causeway distinguish it from the Biomuseo alternative. One tour makes Panama a self-contained destination for several days, while the other gives it the closing section of a broader Central American itinerary.

Some commercial details of the longer tour require separate confirmation: descriptions of hotel-night allocation and the inclusion of domestic flights in the total price contain discrepancies. Check the updated quote and itinerary before booking. Flights appearing in the day-by-day route do not prove that tickets are already included.

## Preparing for the final day

Coordinate the Miraflores visit with current screening times and opportunities to watch ships pass through. The canal remains operating transport infrastructure; vessel movements and the accessibility of certain viewpoints depend on its daily operations. If seeing ships use the locks is the main objective, do not assume every visiting hour offers the same experience.

The extended city tour combines vehicle transfers, walks and indoor exhibitions. Exposed parts of Panama City are usually warm and humid, with potentially heavy rainfall. Comfortable shoes and rain protection are useful, particularly before a long international flight.

For independent comparisons, browse [Panama tours](/panama/tour/) and [multi-country journeys](/multi-country/), but if you specifically want the IMAX film and Amador, confirm inclusion of **this exact excursion**.

## Frequently asked questions about tours with Miraflores and IMAX

### On which day does the excursion take place?

On the [26-day Central America tour](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/), it is scheduled for **day 26, the final day**, followed by the flight home.

### How long is the program?

The standalone excursion description gives a duration of **six hours**. The day's plan must also allow time for the airport transfer and check-in.

### Does it include an IMAX film?

Yes. The program specifies a **45-minute film** about the Panama Canal in English with Spanish subtitles. Availability of a particular screening is confirmed for the excursion date.

### Is Biomuseo included?

No. The confirmed itinerary covers IMAX, Miraflores, Casco Antiguo and Amador. The [Biomuseo version](/panama/panama-city/panama-miraflores-biomuseo-casco-viejo/) is a separate excursion product.

## Panama City sightseeing: from Panamá Viejo to Miraflores Locks

[Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/) brings together Spanish colonial ruins, a restored historic center, modern skyscrapers and the engineering works of the Panama Canal. Our excursion connects these different areas in one route with a **Russian-speaking guide**.

The excursion costs **$188**, and the minimum group is **two people**. Stops include Panamá Viejo, Casco Antiguo, Ancon Hill, the Amador Causeway, the Miraflores visitor center and Balboa Avenue. The precise duration and individual included tickets are not specified in the excursion's terms.

## Panamá Viejo and Casco Antiguo: two historic centers

**Panamá Viejo** consists of the ruins of the original Spanish colonial settlement beside the Pacific. After the original town was destroyed, its center was moved to a new section of the coastline. This created **Casco Antiguo**, a fortified district preserving colonial squares, churches and residences. UNESCO regards the two areas as parts of Panama's historic heritage.

During a walk through Casco Antiguo, travelers can see the Presidential Palace, Cathedral Square, National Theatre and Plaza de Francia. San José Church, Plaza Bolívar and the Las Bóvedas complex also feature in the program. Together they illustrate the city's commercial history, defenses and changing public life.

The inclusion of a building in the itinerary does not automatically mean visitors enter it. Admission tickets and indoor guided visits depend on the selected program and the rules of each site.

## Ancon Hill and the Causeway: two perspectives on the city

Ancon Hill is a viewpoint overlooking the city and canal area. **Amador Causeway** connects former islands near the canal's Pacific entrance and provides a different view of Panama City's modern high-rise districts. It helps explain how canal construction changed the shoreline and transport links.

The contrast with Casco Antiguo is immediately visible: colonial squares and low buildings give way to wide roads, residential districts and modern skylines.

## Miraflores: how the Panama Canal locks work

**Miraflores Locks** are an engineering installation where water levels are adjusted to allow ships through. Visitors to the observation platform may watch vessels passing when ships are present. Our route also includes the visitor center, a museum display and a film about the canal's construction.

However, the order of the visit, current museum access and admission prices need to be checked for the travel date. Shipping schedules and specific transit times do not guarantee that a large cruise ship will be visible at any given moment.

## Excursion terms and choosing your route

The excursion includes **Russian-speaking guidance**, costs **$188**, and requires a group of at least two people. The guide may recommend a lunch restaurant according to guests' preferences. Lunch itself is not listed as a paid included service, so its cost needs to be agreed separately.

| Detail | Program |
|---|---|
| Minimum group | 2 people |
| Language | Russian |
| Price | $188 |
| Main theme | History and the canal |

## Frequently asked questions about Panama City sightseeing

### What's the difference between Panamá Viejo and Casco Antiguo?

Panamá Viejo is the site of the original colonial town, while Casco Antiguo is the historic center established after the town was relocated.

### Can I see ships at Miraflores?

Yes, viewing the locks is part of the route, but actual ship movements depend on the canal's schedule.

### Is lunch included?

The guide can suggest a restaurant; a paid lunch is not listed among the included services.

### How much is the excursion?

The Ada Tours listing gives $188 and a minimum group of two travelers. The basis of this price should be clarified when booking.

## Miraflores, Biomuseo and Casco Viejo: three sides of Panama City in one day

The itinerary combines three major themes of [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/): the engineering history of the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/), Central America's nature and the architecture of the old town. Visiting [Miraflores Locks](/panama/place/miraflores-locks/) reveals how ships pass between different water levels. [Biomuseo](/panama/place/biomuseo/) explains the connection between Panama's geography and its biodiversity. [Casco Viejo](/panama/place/casco-viejo/) introduces the city's history through its streets, squares and buildings.

Ada Tours includes this excursion on day two of its [six-day “Panama City and Gamboa” tour](/panama/tour/panama-city-gamboa-6-days/). Travelers begin at Miraflores, then visit Biomuseo, take a walking tour of Casco Viejo after lunch and return to their hotel. Separate booking terms and the guiding language are agreed individually.

## Miraflores: how the Panama Canal operates

Miraflores is one of the best-known places to learn about the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/). The lock system allows ships to overcome differences in elevation between the ocean and the inland water system. Understanding how it works explains why the canal transformed shipping and the country's history.

The visitor center is beside the locks, where travelers can learn about the waterway and observe shipping when conditions allow. **The passage of any particular ship does not follow a fixed excursion timetable**, so neither the number nor the size of vessels visible can be guaranteed. Available parts of the visitor center and its opening arrangements also need to be confirmed before travel: modernization work and visitor rules may change.

This stop focuses on engineering. For observing the forested banks and wildlife from the water, the [Gatun Lake and Monkey Island boat excursion](/panama/gatun-lake/gatun-lake-monkey-island-boat/), included on another day of the same tour, is more suitable.

## Biomuseo: why Panama has such diverse nature

[Biomuseo](/panama/place/biomuseo/) is known for its brightly colored roofs, designed by architect Frank Gehry. Its exhibitions explore Panama's biodiversity and the geological processes that formed the Isthmus of Panama and transformed connections between natural regions in the Americas.

After Miraflores, this stop reveals another perspective on the canal and Panama itself. The locks demonstrate human-made infrastructure; the museum explains how land formed and how plants and animals came to inhabit it. The architecture is an attraction in its own right, with large colorful roof planes clearly visible outside.

Temporary exhibitions, open galleries and the language of the museum's materials can change. We do not promise a specific temporary show or a private guided tour of every gallery. If a particular topic matters to you, check that its exhibition areas will be available on your travel date.

## Casco Viejo: the historic quarter and a walk after lunch

[Casco Viejo](/panama/place/casco-viejo/) is the capital's historic quarter and forms part of a UNESCO World Heritage property. It preserves old churches, squares, balcony-fronted facades and buildings from different periods, including colonial and French-influenced architecture.

Our program's walk through the neighborhood takes place **after lunch**. This is a good way to explore the city on foot: the streets and squares reveal the contrast between old architecture and the modern capital. The precise duration, order of stops and churches entered are not fixed in advance.

Casco Viejo should not be confused with the archaeological site of Panamá Viejo: they differ in location and history. This excursion explicitly includes the historic Casco Viejo quarter.

## Preparing for a busy day of city sightseeing

The route combines an engineering site, a museum and a walk. Comfortable shoes are useful in Casco Viejo, together with water, a hat and sunscreen in the heat. Rain is possible in exposed areas, so a light rain jacket or compact umbrella may also be useful.

If traveling with children or a person with limited mobility, discuss the walking sections and accessibility of museum spaces in advance. Travel between stops, entry queues and traffic affect the actual schedule. The total guaranteed duration and precise admission tickets in a separately sold excursion have not been confirmed.

On the [“Panama City and Gamboa” tour](/panama/tour/panama-city-gamboa-6-days/), this city day is followed by a visit to an Emberá community and then nature excursions near Gamboa. For travelers choosing primarily historical attractions, the [Culture and History theme](/interests/culture-and-history/) is a useful starting point.

## Frequently asked questions about the Panama City excursion

### Can we see a ship passing through Miraflores?

The locks are used by ships, but the passage of a particular vessel at a scheduled time is not guaranteed. Available viewpoints and visitor center hours are confirmed for the date of the visit.

### Which places are included in Ada Tours' route?

Miraflores, Biomuseo and an afternoon walk through Casco Viejo are confirmed. These are the stops listed in the [six-day program](/panama/tour/panama-city-gamboa-6-days/).

### Should we allow time for walking?

Yes. Casco Viejo is explored on foot through streets and historic squares. Let us know about any mobility limitations before agreeing on the excursion.

### Is the excursion included in the tour price?

It is included in the named tour's program. Separate-booking terms, guide language and the exact list of included services must be agreed individually.

### Are Biomuseo and Casco Viejo in the same building?

No. [Biomuseo](/panama/place/biomuseo/) and the [Casco Viejo historic quarter](/panama/place/casco-viejo/) are separate stops in different parts of the capital.

## Tours including the Miraflores, Biomuseo and Casco Viejo excursion

**The [six-day “Panama City and Gamboa” journey](/panama/tour/panama-city-gamboa-6-days/) includes the specific [Miraflores, Biomuseo and Casco Viejo excursion](/panama/panama-city/panama-miraflores-biomuseo-casco-viejo/).** It brings together the Panama Canal's engineering history, the country's natural heritage and the capital's historic quarter. This is a convenient first introduction to [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/), as each of the three stops offers something different.

The standalone excursion description does not specify a fixed individual price or guaranteed guide language; terms are agreed separately. Within the six-day tour, the excursion is part of an established itinerary with accommodation and other days around the capital. The terms of the entire tour cannot automatically be applied to a separately booked excursion.

## What the three parts of the excursion show

### Miraflores Locks: how the canal works

The first stop is [Miraflores Locks](/panama/place/miraflores-locks/), part of the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/) system. At the visitor center, travelers learn about the history of the waterway and lock mechanisms and may watch ships transit. It is one of the clearest ways to understand the canal's influence on Panama's development and international trade.

Visiting Miraflores visitor center and sailing through the canal are two distinct travel products. This excursion includes viewing the complex and learning how it operates, not a separate cruise through the canal.

### Biomuseo: Panama's natural history

The next stop is [Biomuseo](/panama/place/biomuseo/), designed by Frank Gehry. Its exhibitions explore the country's biodiversity and the formation of natural landscapes on the Isthmus of Panama. This provides a transition from the canal's engineering story to the tropical forests featured on subsequent days.

Unlike watching wildlife outdoors, the museum introduces Panama's geography through exhibits. Visiting the museum building does not imply an excursion to a national park.

### Casco Viejo: history of the old town

After lunch, the itinerary includes a walking tour of [Casco Viejo](/panama/place/casco-viejo/), Panama City's historic quarter. Its squares, old churches and architecture influenced by colonial and French styles are highlights. The streets and public spaces reveal the capital beyond its modern high-rise districts.

| Stop | Main theme |
|---|---|
| Miraflores | Locks and shipping |
| Biomuseo | Panama's biodiversity |
| Casco Viejo | History and architecture |

## How the excursion fits into the six-day tour

The [six-day program](/panama/tour/panama-city-gamboa-6-days/) begins in the capital. **On day two**, after breakfast, travelers visit Miraflores, Biomuseo and the historic center. A walk through Casco Viejo follows lunch, and the evening ends with a return to the Panama City hotel.

On the following day, the setting changes: a canoe trip along the Chagres River and a visit to an Emberá community, followed by a transfer to Gamboa. Other days focus on forested natural areas rather than only city landmarks. This tour therefore suits people who want to experience both the canal's engineering heritage and tropical landscapes.

The city day introduces the trip. It is less physically demanding than some nature walks, but it includes several visits and transfers. Comfortable shoes are needed in the old town, while the capital's heat and possible rain should be considered.

## Choosing one excursion day or a six-day journey

If your primary interest is the canal and the capital's architecture, the [standalone excursion](/panama/panama-city/panama-miraflores-biomuseo-casco-viejo/) covers all three stops without purchasing a multi-day tour. Separate service terms are agreed before booking.

If you want to explore the tropical forest, Chagres River and Gamboa's natural areas afterward, look at the [complete six-day itinerary](/panama/tour/panama-city-gamboa-6-days/). Here the city and nature sections form a continuous journey. Other [Panama tours](/panama/tour/) may pass through the canal, but that does not prove they include this exact excursion with Biomuseo and Casco Viejo.

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring Miraflores and Biomuseo

### Which excursion is included on day two of the six-day tour?

Day two lists Miraflores Locks, Biomuseo and a walk through Casco Viejo. The [excursion description](/panama/panama-city/panama-miraflores-biomuseo-casco-viejo/) covers canal history, Panama's nature and the old town's architecture.

### Can the canal be visited without the Casco Viejo excursion?

That depends on the chosen product. In this itinerary the stops form one excursion day; separate booking and its conditions require agreement. Other canal visit formats may have different content.

### Does the six-day tour include nature excursions?

Yes. After the capital, the route continues to the Chagres River, an Emberá community and Gamboa. Check the [full tour program](/panama/tour/panama-city-gamboa-6-days/) for the contents of each nature day, because they are distinct travel stages.
